chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hakim al-Khas'ami, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding the woman who has despaired of menstruation (menopause), if her husband divorces her, he said: 'She has become divorced from him, and there is no waiting period (Iddah) upon her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a menopausal woman after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a menopausal woman (Al-Mu'assah), the divorce is effective immediately upon pronouncement without the need for a waiting period (Iddah), distinguishing her status from menstruating women. This ruling, derived from the Quranic verse on divorce, underscores the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital dissolution for women who have ceased menstruation, ensuring clarity in their legal capacity to remarry.
